plans.note: No standalone limitation of liability heading in the outline; a cap or disclaimer is most often folded into the indemnity section (sec-12). Numbering gaps (3, 4, 6, 9, 11) suggest unlisted sections may also carry a liability clause — confirm before concluding it is missing.

Sec-12 is the operative indemnity. Check direction: as Client we need TrueLink's IP/misconduct indemnity, and we must keep our own indemnity narrow — sec-7 (unsolicited e-mail) and sec-8 (Client covenants/warranties) are likely hooks for a broad Client-side indemnity.
Restrictions on the businesses we may run would sit in sec-8 (Client covenants) or as a field-of-use limit in sec-2 (License). Likely absent, but sec-8 must be read in full.
Any obligation to source hosting or licensed technology solely from TrueLink would appear in the licence grant (sec-2) or Client covenants (sec-8); pricing-linked exclusivity could sit in sec-5.
Any most-favoured-pricing language would be in Compensation (sec-5). Only flag if it runs against us (we owe TrueLink best terms); an MFN in our favour is welcome.
Employee non-solicits are commonly appended to Client covenants (sec-8) or the confidentiality section (sec-10). Check for duration and a general-advertising carve-out if present.

No term/termination heading appears in the supplied outline; sections 3, 4, 6, 9 and 11 are not listed, so termination rights may live in an unlisted section. Treat as absent from the reviewable text unless those sections surface.
Renewal term and price-escalation mechanics would normally accompany a term clause (not in the outline) or the fee schedule in sec-5. Verify sec-5 for renewal pricing before concluding it is missing.
No general/miscellaneous section is listed; governing law and venue are presumably in an unlisted trailing section. Flag as missing from the reviewable text and ask for the balance of the agreement.
Assignment/change-of-control is usually in miscellaneous (not in the outline); a non-transferability restriction may also be embedded in the licence grant at sec-2 — check that first.

Ownership language should sit in sec-2 (License) with supporting definitions in sec-1; confirm that Client data, content and any hosted materials remain ours and that nothing assigns our marks or data to TrueLink. Sec-10 may govern data as Confidential Information.
Sec-2 is the licence grant; test scope for affiliate/contractor use and for revocability at will, reading grant-related defined terms in sec-1 (including Hosting Services).
Usage or records audits against Client would most likely be attached to Compensation (sec-5) or Client covenants (sec-8). If present, check notice, frequency, location and cost allocation.
Sec-7 (unsolicited commercial e-mail) is a likely home for per-message penalties or fixed damages payable by Client; sec-5 may carry late fees or fixed charges. Only flag amounts running against us.

The only warranty heading in the outline is Client-side (sec-8); a TrueLink performance/hosting warranty and any disclaimer may sit in an unlisted section. Read sec-8 to confirm the warranty burden is not one-directional.
No insurance heading appears anywhere in the outline; TrueLink hosts our site and touches Client data, so raise the standard insurance package as a gap.
Any minimum fee, take-or-pay or volume floor would be in Compensation (sec-5). Check for guaranteed monthly minimums before treating as absent.

No termination or wind-down section is listed; sec-10 may only require return/destruction of Confidential Information, which is not a substitute for data return in usable format plus migration assistance.
